# TUI action reference

This file is generated from the action, mutation and command-disposition catalogues that
drive the live TUI. Run `cargo xtask tui-reference` after changing one of those catalogues.

Live `?` help uses the same action membership and key bindings, then adds the current
context, availability and exact reason for a disabled action. `Ctrl-P` searches these
actions, every mutation below and the explicit CLI boundaries. Key repeats are accepted
only for navigation actions; confirmation and mutation actions require a fresh press.

## Shell actions

| Keys | Action | Context |
|---|---|---|
| `Esc` | Back or cancel | global; reverses the current layer or history |
| `q/C-c` | Quit safely | global base shell |
| `i` | Build identity and capabilities | global |
| `1` | Open Overview | global destination |
| `2` | Open Tasks | global destination |
| `3` | Open Diagnostics | global destination |
| `4` | Open Graph | global destination |
| `5` | Open Reports | global destination |
| `6` | Open Inbox | global destination |
| `C-n` | Quick capture | global loaded shell |
| `Tab` | Focus next region | loaded shell |
| `S-Tab` | Focus previous region | loaded shell |
| `down/j` | Move to next item or down | lists, overlays and Graph |
| `up/k` | Move to previous item or up | lists, overlays and Graph |
| `Enter` | Open or drill into selection | focused selectable content |
| `/` | Search current destination | Tasks, Inbox, Diagnostics, Graph or Reports |
| `d` | Edit clock or cycle graph direction | Due/Stale contexts or Graph |
| `f` | Edit structured filters | Tasks, Inbox, Diagnostics or Graph |
| `s` | Cycle ordering or grouping | Tasks, Diagnostics or Graph |
| `w` | Toggle blocking explanation depth | task Work inspector |

## Mutation actions

Mutations are found by title or CLI name in `Ctrl-P`. Each opens a typed form or preview;
nothing is published until the guarded confirmation step succeeds.

| Palette action | CLI semantics |
|---|---|
| Quick capture | `aplan capture` |
| Amend capture | `aplan inbox amend` |
| Discard capture | `aplan inbox discard` |
| Restore capture | `aplan inbox restore` |
| Promote capture to task | `aplan inbox promote` |
| Claim task | `aplan claim` |
| Release claim | `aplan release` |
| Start task | `aplan start` |
| Stop task | `aplan stop` |
| Add blocking dependency | `aplan dep add` |
| Remove blocking dependency | `aplan dep rm` |
| Add ordering preference | `aplan dep add --prefer` |
| Remove ordering preference | `aplan dep rm --prefer` |
| Add task tag | `aplan tag add` |
| Remove task tag | `aplan tag rm` |
| Rename tag across plan | `aplan tag rename` |
| Move tasks | `aplan mv` |
| Drop tasks | `aplan drop` |
| Drop cuts and live members | `aplan drop --cut` |
| Add task | `aplan add` |
| Add tasks from manifest | `aplan add --from` |
| Import proposal tasks | `aplan import` |
| Supersede completed outcome | `aplan supersede` |
| Rekey task | `aplan rekey` |
| Close task with evidence | `aplan close` |
| Add evidence to closed task | `aplan amend --add-evidence` |
| Replace evidence on closed task | `aplan amend --replace-evidence` |
| Remove evidence from closed task | `aplan amend --remove-evidence` |
| Review and restamp baselines | `aplan close --restamp` |
| Apply verification repairs | `aplan verify --fix` |

## Guided and CLI-only boundaries

These entries are deliberately inert in the TUI. Searching `Ctrl-P` or `?` shows the
same reason and exact copyable command rather than implying that the full-screen surface
performed a batch, transport, alternate-root or automation operation.

### `check --traces-root` (CLI-only)

the interactive advanced check can use or disable the loaded trace root, but selecting a different filesystem root remains an explicit CLI session boundary

```sh
aplan check --traces-root .
```

### `verify --repo` (CLI-only)

the interactive verifier is bound to the loaded repository identity; selecting another evidence repository requires an explicit CLI invocation

```sh
aplan verify --repo .
```

### `verify --no-require-effort` (CLI-only)

the interactive verifier reports the loaded effort policy but does not weaken it for one run; that override remains explicit at the CLI boundary

```sh
aplan verify --no-require-effort
```

### `verify --traces-root` (CLI-only)

the interactive verifier is bound to the loaded trace policy and root; selecting another trace root remains an explicit CLI session boundary

```sh
aplan verify --traces-root .
```

### `verify --no-traces` (CLI-only)

the interactive verifier reports the loaded trace policy but does not disable trace validation for one run; that override remains explicit at the CLI boundary

```sh
aplan verify --no-traces
```

### `verify --deny-warnings` (CLI-only)

the interactive verifier uses the loaded warning verdict and does not strengthen it for one run; that override remains explicit at the CLI boundary

```sh
aplan verify --deny-warnings
```

### `verify --no-deny-warnings` (CLI-only)

the interactive verifier uses the loaded warning verdict and does not weaken it for one run; that override remains explicit at the CLI boundary

```sh
aplan verify --no-deny-warnings
```

### `verify --test-receipts` (CLI-only)

receipt import is a caller-owned path and trust boundary assembled by automation, so the interactive verifier displays retained provenance but does not select a manifest

```sh
aplan verify --test-receipts receipts.json
```

### `verify --refresh-test-receipts` (CLI-only)

receipt refresh publishes an automation artifact against explicit Git revisions, so its set, base and head remain one deliberate CLI workflow

```sh
aplan verify --refresh-test-receipts receipts.json --refresh-base HEAD~1 --refresh-head HEAD
```

### `verify --refresh-working-tree` (CLI-only)

refreshing receipts from index and working-tree bytes is an explicit automation boundary rather than an action inferred from the loaded interactive snapshot

```sh
aplan verify --refresh-working-tree --refresh-test-receipts receipts.json --refresh-base HEAD
```

### `verify --refresh-shadow` (CLI-only)

the complete direct shadow oracle can execute every configured provider and remains an explicit trust-bearing automation invocation

```sh
aplan verify --refresh-shadow --refresh-test-receipts receipts.json --refresh-base HEAD~1 --refresh-head HEAD
```

### `test receipt` (CLI-only)

receipt production executes one configured provider and binds external CI provenance, so it remains an explicit automation boundary rather than an interactive catalogue search

```sh
aplan test receipt --help
```

### `tui` (entry point)

this command starts the current interface and cannot recursively appear as an invokable action inside itself

```sh
aplan tui
```

### `attest` (CLI-only)

attestation is a clean-commit batch artifact, and optional git-note attachment belongs to the explicit command boundary

```sh
aplan attest --no-config
```

### `export-agents-md` (CLI-only)

generated-document stdout, write and check modes are deterministic batch contracts rather than interactive plan actions

```sh
aplan export-agents-md --check AGENTS.md
```

### `export-roadmap-json` (CLI-only)

the foreign roadmap file is both template and output, so its explicit path and check/write contract remain a batch workflow

```sh
aplan export-roadmap-json --check roadmap.json
```

### `export` (CLI-only)

serialized stdout and file output are intended for pipes and generated artifacts rather than the full-screen renderer

```sh
aplan export --format checklist
```

### `park` (CLI-only)

portfolio parking is an all-or-none claim-aware batch whose shared reason, optional schedule and tags require one explicit command until the TUI has a complete batch review form

```sh
aplan park T-123 --reason "deferred until the next cycle"
```

### `unpark` (CLI-only)

portfolio unparking is an all-or-none claim-aware batch that clears scheduling metadata, so it remains an explicit command until the TUI can review the complete target set

```sh
aplan unpark T-123
```

### `blueprint` (CLI-only)

blueprint application captures a caller-selected local file and renders its complete predicted graph before an explicit guarded batch write, so it remains a copyable command until the TUI has a file picker and full multi-task review form

```sh
aplan blueprint apply --file feature.yml --cut M-next --dry-run
```

### `mcp` (CLI-only)

the MCP server owns standard input and output as a long-running machine transport rather than an interactive plan action

```sh
aplan mcp
```

### `init` (guided)

setup renders the selected target and a non-overwriting command, then retries discovery after the user performs it

```sh
aplan init .
```

### `facts` (guided)

About renders the typed capability document and build identity without duplicating the machine-oriented assertion mode

```sh
aplan facts --identity
```

### `facts --require` (CLI-only)

About displays the typed capability inventory, while a process-exit assertion for automation remains an explicit machine-oriented CLI boundary

```sh
aplan facts --require build.tui
```

### `schema` (CLI-only)

schema output is a machine-consumed stdout artifact whose exact serialization is the purpose of the command

```sh
aplan schema
```
